thread_title: S. leucophylla 'DARK RED' Franklin Co, FL
breadcrumb: S. leucophylla 'DARK RED' Franklin Co, FL

posts.body_html:
Out of more than 200 seedlings, this one individual stood out from the rest because it has the darkest red color! In person, the color appears more of a purple-ish red, the camera slightly altered the actual color. Nevertheless, You can still tell it's pretty dark from these photos. I wouldn't be surprised if this clone turns dark purple under a "greenhouse suntan" Who knows, maybe it can do this outdoors too?

posts.body_html: Very nice! About the greenhouse suntan...I experience the exact opposite. Plants outside are much more colorful than plants in the GH. Thoughts?
posts.body_text: Very nice! About the greenhouse suntan...I experience the exact opposite. Plants outside are much more colorful than plants in the GH. Thoughts?

posts.body_html: That is absolutely peculiar Eric, thanks for sharing your results with us!  Only thing I can think of is that your grow season weather outdoors is pretty close to what it's like in the wild.  Plants in the wild get as colorful as can be.  On the pacific Northwest, plants grown in greenhouses compared to outdoors are much warmer on average (both day and night), more humid, and some light rays that otherwise bleach out anthocyanins  are filtered out.
